sections.text: The paid Travel Certificate proves travel for reimbursement, GST or LTC purposes. Do not treat it as a delay or cancellation certificate; ask the airline which evidence it can provide. faq.q: What should I do if my IndiGo baggage is damaged or missing?
faq.a: Report to the staff in the destination arrival hall before leaving the airport. Keep your baggage tag, boarding pass, and all records.

faq.q: What is the deadline for delayed baggage claims on IndiGo?
faq.a: Written notice for delayed baggage must be given within 21 days from the date the baggage is made available to you, not from the flight arrival date.

faq.q: Is IndiGo's paid Travel Certificate the same as a delay certificate?
faq.a: No. The paid Travel Certificate is proof of travel, not a delay or cancellation certificate. Insurance claims are assessed separately under your policy terms.

faq.q: How do I get a flight certificate from Thai Airways?
faq.a: Thai Airways publishes an official flight-certificate guide. For delays over 15 minutes on arrival, certificates can be requested from 3 days to 6 months after the scheduled travel date. This applies to actual Thai Airways operated flights; for codeshare flights, check with the actual operating carrier.

faq.q: What are Thai Airways' baggage claim deadlines?
faq.a: For damaged baggage: written notice within 7 days of arrival. For delayed baggage: within 21 days of receiving the baggage. File a PIR at the airport and keep actual expense receipts as proof.

faq.q: Does the airline certificate guarantee my insurance claim?
faq.a: No. The certificate documents the disruption. Insurance claims are assessed separately under your policy — the airline document does not mean automatic approval.

guides.title: Air India delay or cancellation proof for an insurance claim
guides.description: Request the free Flight Disruption Statement for an eligible Air India-operated flight.
guides.text: Use Air India’s Flight Disruption Statement when your insurer asks for documentary evidence of a delay, cancellation or diversion. The airline provides this statement free of charge.

sections.title: Check eligibility and flight details
sections.text: The official page covers Air India-operated disrupted flights in the past six months. Its issue condition is 24 hours after flight arrival, and a delayed flight must have arrived more than 15 minutes late. Enter the flight number, travel date, origin and destination; follow the official email verification instructions.

sections.title: A Travel Certificate is a different document
sections.text: The paid Travel Certificate proves completed travel for reimbursement or LTC claims. It is separate from the free Flight Disruption Statement. Check the document name requested by your insurer before choosing the application.

faq.q: Is the delay statement free?
faq.a: Yes. Air India’s official page says no payment is required for the Flight Disruption Statement.

faq.q: Is the Travel Certificate the same proof?
faq.a: No. It proves completed travel and is a separate paid service. For disruption evidence, use the Flight Disruption Statement.

guides.title: Delay and cancellation rights for flights departing Thailand: CAAT complaints
guides.description: Check assistance, compensation conditions and the official CAAT complaint route when a scheduled international flight departing Thailand is delayed or cancelled.
guides.text:
For a scheduled international flight departing a Thai airport such as Suvarnabhumi or Don Mueang, check the passenger protection rules in CAB Regulation No. 101 described by CAAT, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand. Both Thai and foreign airlines fall within this scope. Do not apply this departure-based scope unchanged to flights departing another country.
The regulation took effect on 20 May 2025. The guidance below concerns scheduled international flights departing Thailand; check separate rules for domestic and charter flights. Insurance claims and statutory airline assistance or compensation have different points of contact.
sources: https://www.caat.or.th/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/ข้อบังคับของคณะกรรมการการบินพลเรือน-ฉบับที่-๑๐๑.pdf

sections.title: Check the check-in conditions
sections.text:
Article 10 of CAB Regulation No. 101 covers, among others, passengers who check in within the time notified by the airline. If no separate check-in time is notified for an international flight, the reference is at least one hour before scheduled departure; the regulation also includes cases where the airline accepts check-in at another time.
Passengers transferred to another flight, whose schedule changes by more than five hours from scheduled departure, or whose booked flight is cancelled are also addressed separately. A delay notification does not automatically extend the check-in deadline; confirm with the airline.

sections.title: How is the delay measured?
sections.text:
CAAT guidance measures an ordinary delay by departure. It runs from the approved scheduled departure time, or the time notified at purchase, until the aircraft doors close. Conditions also allow the revised time to be used when a schedule change is notified at least 24 hours in advance, so keep both the original schedule and the change notification.
For waiting on the ground after the doors close, check the separate tarmac delay provisions. Do not confuse actual take-off time, arrival delay or an airline certificate’s issue conditions with this page’s ordinary delay calculation.

sections.title: Assistance you can request by delay length
sections.text: Every threshold below means more than the stated duration. Start by requesting meals, refreshments and communication; for a long wait, check accommodation, transfers and the refund option if you decide not to continue travelling. Separate exceptions apply to financial compensation.

sections.title: Distance-based compensation for delays over ten hours and international cancellations
sections.text: The regulation sets financial compensation at THB 2,000 for distances up to 1,500 km, THB 3,500 for distances over 1,500 km and up to 3,500 km, and THB 4,500 for distances over 3,500 km. The same distance bands apply to international cancellations, subject to exceptions. Do not automatically add the THB 1,500 for a delay over five hours; ask the airline which stage and amount apply.

sections.title: Choose a refund or alternative travel after cancellation
sections.text: Ask the airline about a refund of fares and fees for the unused journey and the choice of an alternative flight. Check meals and communication assistance too. If the alternative flight departs more than one day after the original departure time, the regulation includes necessary accommodation and transfers between the airport and accommodation. For a voucher, its conditions must be explained and you must agree.

sections.title: Financial compensation can have exceptions
sections.text: Extraordinary circumstances demonstrated by the airline can be an exception to financial compensation for delay or cancellation. International cancellation exceptions also include notice at least seven days in advance with other travel options, or later notice where the alternative flight reaches the destination no more than three hours earlier or later than originally scheduled. These are financial compensation exceptions; check meals, alternative travel and refunds separately rather than assuming that all support is unavailable.

sections.title: What to ask the airline at the airport
sections.text: Check the operating carrier, date and flight number on your ticket, and ask for the delay or cancellation reason and passenger rights information in writing. Specify the meal vouchers, accommodation, refund or alternative flight you need to make your request easier to process. Keep delay notices, the original and revised schedules, reference numbers and receipts. Request financial compensation, expense reimbursement and ticket refunds separately.

sections.title: Collect evidence for airline requests and complaints
sections.text:
Use your booking confirmation, e-ticket and boarding pass to check the operating carrier, flight number, departure date and original departure time. Keeping airline delay or cancellation notices, revised schedules and delay or cancellation certificates helps explain what happened.
Record your requests for meals, accommodation, refunds, alternative flights or compensation, together with replies and reference numbers. Keep itemised receipts for anything you paid yourself. This is preparation guidance and does not replace the mandatory document list shown by the CAAT complaint system or requested by the airline. For insurance claims, check your insurer’s policy and document instructions separately.

sections.title: Open the official CAAT complaint website
sections.text: If the airline has not provided your prescribed rights, use the official CAAT complaint website. It currently redirects to the CAAT authentication login page. Choose English in the language menu at the top to see Email / User Name, Password and Sign In in English. Choose Sign Up if you do not have an account, or Forgot password? if you have forgotten your password. Follow the official system’s instructions for submission fields and evidence after login.

sections.title: Distinguish refund deadlines from compensation payment deadlines
sections.text: Fare refund deadlines run from receipt of a complete application and the related documents. The regulation specifies 14 days for cash purchases directly from the airline, 45 days for credit card purchases, and 60 days for agent purchases from complete receipt by the relevant airline or agent. Financial compensation for international delays over five or ten hours uses 14 days from the delayed flight’s date, which differs from the refund deadline.

sections.title: Original regulation and source check date
sections.text: The source check date is 13 October 2026. The basis is CAB Regulation No. 101 and CAAT’s official passenger rights guidance. CAAT’s published English translation and explanations are for reference; for a dispute, check the original Thai regulation together with the facts of the flight.

sections.title: Tarmac waits and leaving the aircraft
sections.text: After a tarmac wait exceeding three hours, disembarkation applies if the take-off time remains undetermined, subject to safety, security and air traffic control exceptions.
sources: https://www.caat.or.th/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/ข้อบังคับของคณะกรรมการการบินพลเรือน-ฉบับที่-๑๐๑.pdf

sections.title: Agreed non-cash fare refunds
sections.text: An agreed voucher or credit fare refund is due within seven days after receipt of the complete application and documents, with its conditions explained.
sources: https://www.caat.or.th/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/ข้อบังคับของคณะกรรมการการบินพลเรือน-ฉบับที่-๑๐๑.pdf

sections.title: If your cabin class changes
sections.text: Article 9 requires your agreement when the airline changes your cabin class. An upgrade by the airline must not incur additional charges. For a downgrade, the fare refund is 30% for flights up to 1,500 km, 50% over 1,500 km and up to 3,500 km, and 75% over 3,500 km. Articles 18 and 19 govern refund procedures and timing.
sources: https://www.caat.or.th/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/ข้อบังคับของคณะกรรมการการบินพลเรือน-ฉบับที่-๑๐๑.pdf

sections.title: Optional extras and other rights
sections.text: Check the actual operating airline and total price. Paid extras require prior opt-in consent. Baggage claims under Article 6 follow international air carriage law. Articles 24 and 25 preserve more favourable protection and other legal compensation rights.
sources: https://www.caat.or.th/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/ข้อบังคับของคณะกรรมการการบินพลเรือน-ฉบับที่-๑๐๑.pdf

thresholds.label: More than two hours
thresholds.text: Meals, refreshments or meal vouchers appropriate to the waiting time, and necessary means of communication.

thresholds.label: More than five hours
thresholds.text: In addition to meals and communication, THB 1,500 financial compensation, suitable accommodation for at least one night where needed, and airport transfers. Choose a refund of the unused journey if you decide not to continue travelling.

thresholds.label: More than ten hours
thresholds.text: Distance-based financial compensation of THB 2,000, 3,500 or 4,500, meals, communication, necessary accommodation and transfers. Choose a refund of the unused journey or alternative travel.

faq.q: Can CAAT rules apply to a foreign airline departing Thailand?
faq.a: Scheduled international flights departing Thailand fall within the scope whether operated by Thai or foreign airlines. Check the operating carrier and passenger protection conditions for your booked flight.

faq.q: Do the same rules apply to a flight departing another country for Thailand?
faq.a: The international flight rules on this page apply to departures from Thailand. For flights departing another country, check that departure country’s rules and the airline or seller’s guidance separately.

faq.q: Does a five-hour delay always mean THB 1,500 compensation?
faq.a: The regulation specifies THB 1,500 for international delays of more than five hours. Compensation exceptions, including extraordinary circumstances, mean that exactly five hours or an exception cannot be treated in the same way.

faq.q: Does a weather-related cancellation remove every form of assistance?
faq.a: The extraordinary circumstances provisions are exceptions to financial compensation. Ask the airline about meals, refunds, alternative flights and other assistance separately.

faq.q: How do I complain to CAAT?
faq.a: Open the official complaint.caat.or.th website and sign in with a CAAT account. You can select English in the language menu, and Sign Up is available if you do not have an account. Prepare your requests to the airline and evidence of the flight and expenses when submitting a complaint.

faq.q: Is this seven-day deadline for delay compensation?
faq.a: No. Non-cash fare refunds and alternative compensation payments have separate deadlines; the latter uses 14 days.

guides.title: Arriving late at Suvarnabhumi after a flight delay
guides.description: Check Airport Rail Link operating hours and the locations of the 24-hour taxi and Grab pick-up areas before travelling to your accommodation.
guides.text: After immigration and baggage collection, check when you can actually leave the airport. Late at night, you can use the taxi and Grab pick-up areas at Suvarnabhumi’s main terminal.

sections.title: Check Airport Rail Link hours first
sections.text: The official airport guide lists Airport Rail Link operating hours as 05:30–24:00, with the station on basement level 1 of the main terminal. These operating hours are not the last train departure time at each station; check the information on site for the train you need to reach your destination.

sections.title: Finding the public taxi pick-up area on level 1
sections.text: Public taxis operate 24 hours on the inner roadway between gates 4 and 7 on level 1 of the main terminal. Take a queue ticket from the machine and go to the vehicle indicated. Check the cost, allowing for the THB 50 airport surcharge and tolls payable by the passenger. The taxi service desk enquiry number is +66 2 132 0360.

sections.title: Use the designated Grab pick-up area
sections.text: The designated Grab pick-up area is on the outer roadway outside gate 4 on level 1 of the main terminal and operates 24 hours. Book through the app, then check the vehicle shown and the designated location before going there.

sections.title: Notify your accommodation and pre-booked transfer of the change
sections.text: Ask your accommodation whether late check-in is possible and tell your pre-booked transfer provider your revised arrival time. Keep receipts for transport you pay for yourself, but check the flight and insurance policy conditions separately to find out whether the airline or insurer will cover the cost.

faq.q: Can I take Grab if I arrive at Suvarnabhumi after midnight?
faq.a: The official airport guide says the designated Grab pick-up area on the outer roadway outside gate 4 on level 1 of the main terminal operates 24 hours. Check available vehicles and waiting times in the app and on site.

guides.title: Find the right airline counter at the airport
guides.description: Use your operating airline, local departure date and flight number to find the right desk and confirm the day’s check-in arrangements.
guides.text: Start with the operating airline shown on your ticket, the departure date in the departure airport’s local time and your flight number. Then check the airport’s departure screens and the operating airline’s official airport guide.

sections.title: Check the flight before choosing a queue
sections.text: Check which airline actually operates your flight, especially if your ticket also shows another airline’s code. Use the local departure date and flight number to match your flight on the departure screens.

sections.title: Find the departure floor and current counter
sections.text: Follow the departure screens and the operating airline’s official airport information for the terminal, departure floor and check-in area. Counter allocations can change with the season or on the day, so confirm the counter and check-in deadline before joining the queue.

sections.title: Choose the desk for your request
sections.text: Check-in, ticketing and arrivals baggage assistance are different services. For a ticket change or refund request, ask the airline which ticketing or service desk handles it. For a bag that is damaged or has not arrived, ask for the arrivals baggage assistance desk.

sections.title: Confirm the next step with the airline
sections.text: Ask the staff whether the desk handles your request and which documents you need. Delay or cancellation certificates and insurance claims have separate procedures. Finding a ticketing counter does not automatically establish compensation entitlement or mean that the desk pays compensation.

faq.q: Can I use the ticketing counter for a baggage problem?
faq.a: Ticketing and arrivals baggage assistance have different roles. Ask the airline for the desk that handles damaged or missing arrival baggage before joining a queue.

faq.q: Is the counter in the airport guide always the counter for today?
faq.a: Counter allocations can change with the season or on the day. Check your operating airline and flight number on the departure screens, and confirm the counter and check-in deadline with the airline.

faq.q: Can I buy a ticket at a check-in counter?
faq.a: Check-in and ticketing are handled at different counters — confirm each separately. For purchases, use the airlines' offices and official channels.

guides.title: HDFC ERGO Travel Insurance Claims: Documents by Type
guides.description: How to file a travel insurance claim with HDFC ERGO — claim form, documents for delay, baggage and cancellation, and where to submit.
guides.text: Submit your claim to travelclaims@hdfcergo.com with the signed claim form. Documents differ by claim type — check the section for your situation.

sections.title: How to submit
sections.text: Send the signed claim form to travelclaims@hdfcergo.com. For NEFT payment, include a cancelled cheque. The policy-linked proposer completes eKYC. Keep copies of everything — additional documents may be requested.

sections.title: Flight delay
sections.text: Submit signed Section E, the airline's letter stating the duration and cause of delay, your ticket and boarding pass, and receipts for essential expenses directly caused by the delay.

sections.title: Baggage delay vs loss or damage
sections.text: For delayed baggage: signed Section D, original PIR, proof of the delay period, emergency purchase receipts, and airline compensation details. For lost or damaged baggage: signed Section D, original PIR, itemised airline claim, carrier report, baggage tags, passport, and receipts. For both: ticket and boarding pass, baggage tags, passport with India entry and exit records, and airline compensation details.

sections.title: Trip cancellation and coverage
sections.text: For cancellation, provide proof of the reason, prepaid costs, and refund details. Coverage depends on your policy — filing does not guarantee payment.

faq.q: Is an airline certificate enough?
faq.a: No. Use the insurer’s document list for your claim type.

faq.q: Are requirements identical across insurers?
faq.a: No. Check your own policy’s eligibility and insurer’s instructions.

faq.q: Does filing a PIR guarantee my insurance payout?
faq.a: No — the PIR documents the incident, but payout follows your policy wording.

faq.q: Where do I send my HDFC ERGO travel claim?
faq.a: Send the signed claim form and documents to travelclaims@hdfcergo.com.

faq.q: Do baggage delay and baggage loss need the same documents?
faq.a: No. Delay needs proof of the delay period and emergency purchases. Loss or damage needs an itemised airline claim, carrier report, and baggage tags. Both need the original PIR and signed Section D.

faq.q: Will my claim definitely be paid?
faq.a: No. Coverage depends on your policy terms. Additional documents may be requested during review.

guides.title: Thai AirAsia baggage notice deadlines
guides.description: Check the written notice deadline and keep airline correspondence.
guides.text: For checked-baggage damage, FD requires written notice as soon as possible and no later than seven days after receipt. For baggage delay, written notice is due within 21 days after the bag is placed at your disposal, not after flight arrival.

sections.title: Keep statutory rights separate
sections.text: FD’s terms expressly recognise CAB Regulation No. 101 and mandatory laws; assess applicable CAAT rights separately.

faq.q: Does the 21-day period start at flight arrival?
faq.a: No. It starts when the delayed bag is placed at your disposal.

guides.title: ICICI Lombard travel claims
guides.description: Follow your policy and the claim category’s document instructions.
guides.text: These are ICICI Lombard’s published steps, not a benefit guarantee.

sections.title: Report and track
sections.text: Log in with your registered mobile on IL TakeCare or the website. Select your travel policy, Report Claim, then Medical, Baggage & Personal Loss or Others. Upload documents and bank details, submit and track.

sections.title: Delay and baggage documents
sections.text: Carrier delay: bank details, ticket/boarding pass and airline delay-and-reason confirmation. Baggage delay: bank details, ticket/boarding pass and PIR. Damage: photographs and PIR. Loss: bank details and FIR, police report or complaint copy.

sections.title: Missed connection
sections.text: Prepare the initial itinerary, unused-ticket fare, airline refund/no-show details and new-ticket fare.

sections.title: Insurer assistance
sections.text: International callback: +91 124 449 8778; India: 1800 102 5721; USA/Canada: +1 844 871 1200. Email icicilombard@falck.com. These are insurer assistance channels, not airport desks.

faq.q: Are baggage documents identical?
faq.a: No. Follow the relevant category.

faq.q: Does submitting guarantee payment?
faq.a: No. Your policy and claim assessment determine eligibility.

guides.title: Report an IndiGo baggage problem
guides.description: Contact arrival staff and keep the report and airline correspondence.
guides.text: For a missing or damaged bag, contact IndiGo’s desk in the destination arrival hall.

sections.title: Report before leaving
sections.text: IndiGo requires an arrival irregularity report for loss or damage. Its rules treat unreported receipt as evidence of good condition; this is not a statement that every later legal claim is impossible.

sections.title: Delayed-bag notice
sections.text: Notify IndiGo within 21 days after the delayed bag is placed at your disposal, not flight arrival.

sections.title: Keep the record
sections.text: Keep your report and replies, and ask staff about the next step.

faq.q: Is this the check-in counter?
faq.a: No. Use the destination arrival baggage desk.

faq.q: Does the 21-day period start at landing?
faq.a: No. It starts when the delayed bag is available to you.

guides.title: Air India disruption evidence
guides.description: Choose the free disruption statement or paid travel proof.

sections.title: Free disruption statement
sections.text: Air India’s statement covers its operated flights delayed, cancelled or diverted within the past six months. It becomes available 24 hours after arrival; delay means arrival more than 15 minutes late.

sections.title: Request online
sections.text: Enter flight number, travel date, origin and destination. Verify your email to receive the statement. This certificate condition does not establish insurance cover or compensation.

sections.title: Paid completed-travel proof
sections.text: The separate Travel Certificate costs INR 295 per passenger. It covers Air India-issued tickets with all journeys completed within the past year and becomes available 48 hours after the last flight’s departure.

faq.q: Is a disruption statement free?
faq.a: Yes. It is distinct from the paid Travel Certificate.

faq.q: What is the difference between Air India's two certificates?
faq.a: The Flight Disruption Statement is free proof of disruption (delayed, cancelled or diverted AI-operated flights), for the past six months from 24 hours after arrival. The Travel Certificate is paid proof of travel for reimbursement or LTC, for the past year. They are not interchangeable.

guides.text: Choose the free disruption statement or paid travel proof.

guides.title: THAI disruption certificate
guides.description: Request an insurance document through THAI’s official form.
guides.text: Request an insurance document through THAI’s official form.

sections.title: Check eligibility
sections.text: The form covers THAI-operated flights; for codeshares, contact the operating carrier. Its delay condition is arrival more than 15 minutes late.

sections.title: Apply in the stated window
sections.text: Request at least 3 days and no more than 6 months after the scheduled travel date. Passengers or authorised representatives may apply.

sections.title: Prepare documents
sections.text: Provide your passport and travel documents, such as a boarding pass or itinerary, plus the requested passenger and flight details.

faq.q: Does this guarantee insurance payment?
faq.a: No. Certificate eligibility and your policy’s cover are separate.

faq.q: Is it a refund or compensation request?
faq.a: No. Booking changes, refunds and applicable CAAT passenger rights follow separate procedures.

guides.title: THAI damaged baggage
guides.description: Have airport staff assess the damage.
guides.text: Have airport staff assess the damage.

sections.title: Report on arrival
sections.text: Take the damaged bag to THAI baggage staff immediately and obtain a PIR copy.

sections.title: Keep evidence
sections.text: Provide contact details, flight and bag-tag details, and damage evidence. The official page states written claim registration within seven days of arrival.

sections.title: If you have left
sections.text: Contact your local THAI office promptly. Reporting later can make proving the damage harder. Repair or compensation depends on assessment.

faq.q: Is reporting the same as payment?
faq.a: No. Staff assess the damage and claim.

faq.q: Can I also ask my insurer?
faq.a: Yes; check your own policy and retain the airline’s records.

guides.title: THAI delayed baggage
guides.description: Report a missing bag before leaving arrivals.
guides.text: Report a missing bag before leaving arrivals.

sections.title: Open a report
sections.text: Approach THAI ground staff immediately. Give bag details and your contact and delivery address; keep the report copy and file reference.

sections.title: Track delivery
sections.text: Keep your tracing details accurate and notify staff of changes. Delivery is subject to local customs rules.

sections.title: Request expenses separately
sections.text: Submit a written expense claim promptly, no later than 21 days after delivery, with the PIR and receipts. THAI requires actual proven financial loss.

faq.q: Does the 21-day period start at landing?
faq.a: No. This procedure counts from baggage delivery.

faq.q: What should I retain for an expense claim?
faq.a: Keep the PIR and receipts proving the actual financial loss.

guides.title: Arriving late in Phuket
guides.description: Check your airport pickup and onward ride.
guides.text: Allow time for immigration and baggage collection. Tell a booked pickup provider about your delay and revised arrival time.

sections.title: Find the pickup point
sections.text: Grab’s official guide identifies designated pickup points at international arrivals. Confirm your pickup location and hotel address in the app, then follow its directions. Match the vehicle and driver to your booking before boarding.

sections.title: Check availability after dark
sections.text: Check live availability and waiting times. With a pre-booked pickup, confirm that the provider can accommodate your revised arrival.

sections.title: Keep receipts
sections.text: Grab shows upfront fares except for GrabTaxi. Check vehicle type and luggage space. Keep transport receipts and the airline’s delay notice; reimbursement depends on the airline and your policy.

faq.q: Where do I board at international arrivals?
faq.a: Confirm international arrivals in the app and follow its designated pickup directions.

faq.q: Can I leave immediately after landing?
faq.a: Check the actual wait and allow for immigration and baggage collection.

guides.title: Arriving late at Don Mueang
guides.description: Find the taxi desk after international arrivals.
guides.text: Allow for immigration and baggage collection. Tell your hotel and booked pickup provider your revised arrival time.

sections.title: Terminal 1, Gate 8
sections.text: Use the taxi desk on Level 1 at Gate 8 of international Terminal 1. The domestic desk is on Level 1 of the seven-storey parking building beside Terminal 2.

sections.title: Check fares and contacts
sections.text: The metered fare carries a THB 50 airport surcharge; passengers pay expressway tolls. The international taxi desk is 02 535 3653; the public transport management centre is 02 535 1247.

sections.title: Check road conditions
sections.text: The Thai government’s 1 October 2026 notice advises checking destination road conditions at the desk. Ask about alternatives if flooding prevents access. Check train or bus departure times separately and keep transport receipts and the airline’s delay notice.

faq.q: Where is the international taxi desk?
faq.a: Terminal 1, Level 1, Gate 8.

faq.q: Are there extra charges?
faq.a: The airport surcharge is THB 50, with expressway tolls payable by passengers.

guides.title: Find the right IndiGo assistance desk
guides.description: Use your flight details to find the correct airport service.
guides.text: Start with the operating airline, departure-local date and flight number on your ticket.

sections.title: Check-in and ticketing
sections.text: Check departure screens for your flight’s counter. Counter allocations can change seasonally. At Mumbai Terminal 2, the airport lists IndiGo ticketing opposite Departure Gate 7.

sections.title: Arrival baggage help
sections.text: For a missing or damaged bag, contact IndiGo staff at the destination arrival-hall desk before leaving. Ask for a record of your report and the next step.

sections.title: Disruption documents
sections.text: Ask airline staff which delay or cancellation evidence they can issue. The paid Travel Certificate proves travel; it is not identified as a disruption certificate.

faq.q: Can the city reservation office handle my bag at arrivals?
faq.a: Use the destination arrival baggage desk for reporting; the Thailand city representative handles reservations.

faq.q: Is a check-in counter automatically an insurance claims desk?
faq.a: No. Ask about airline evidence and check your insurer’s document requirements separately.

faq.q: How do I find my check-in counter at BKK on the day of travel?
faq.a: Check the airport departure displays or IndiGo's official channels on the day of travel. Counter assignments can change by season.

sections.text: Baggage Protection requires qualifying tickets charged to the eligible card or its linked reward points.

sections.title: Baggage evidence
sections.text: For carrier loss/damage or delay, keep carrier reports, PIR, baggage-check details and compensation records.

faq.q: What does reimbursement preparation include?

faq.q: Is damage certification needed?

guides.title: HDFC ERGO Explorer: product-specific checks
guides.description: Match UIN HDFTIOP24042V022425 and your policy start date.
guides.text: The official index assigns this wording to insurance periods starting 31 December 2024 onwards.

sections.title: Keep products separate
sections.text: TravelX is a separate product; do not apply its terms to Explorer.

sections.title: Checked baggage
sections.text: Loss requires a PIR, tickets/boarding pass and baggage slips.

sections.title: Flight delay
sections.text: Prepare receipts, the boarded flight’s ticket/boarding pass and an airline letter explaining the delay and scheduled/actual times.

faq.q: Does checked-baggage loss cover damage?
faq.a: No; this cover excludes damage and partial loss.

faq.q: Are all journey segments covered for delay?
faq.a: Baggage delay excludes the final return-to-India segment; flight delay excludes the segment finally leaving India and flight cancellation.

guides.title: ICICI Lombard TripSecure+: policy document checks
guides.description: Match UIN ICITIOP27060V032627 to your policy schedule.
guides.text: Use your purchased covers and deductibles, not another product’s checklist.

sections.title: Report missing baggage
sections.text: Keep your ticket/boarding pass and notify the carrier and assistance provider/insurer together.

sections.title: Loss evidence
sections.text: Provide the carrier’s PIR or loss confirmation from an insurer-approved independent agency, plus airline compensation evidence.

sections.title: Delay evidence
sections.text: For baggage delay, retain scheduled/actual delivery confirmation and carrier correspondence.

faq.q: Is PIR the only accepted baggage evidence?
faq.a: This wording also allows confirmation from an insurer-approved independent agency for loss or delay.

faq.q: Does the policy document guarantee a payment?
faq.a: No; your selected cover, deductible, exclusions and claim assessment apply.

guides.title: Air India Express: Reporting Damaged, Delayed or Missing Baggage
guides.description: How to file a baggage report (PIR) with Air India Express at the arrival airport, what documents to keep, and how the 21-day rule works.
guides.text: If your checked baggage is damaged, delayed or does not arrive, report it to the Baggage Desk before you leave the arrival airport and file a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) with supporting documents.

sections.title: File the PIR before leaving the airport
sections.text: Report damaged, delayed or missing checked baggage to the Baggage Desk before you leave the arrival airport. Submit the Property Irregularity Report (PIR) along with supporting documents. This follows the airline's international conditions of carriage, section X(g)(xvii).

sections.title: Documents to keep
sections.text: Keep your baggage tag, a copy of the PIR report, your boarding pass, and receipts for essential purchases. These support both the airline report and any later insurance claim. The airline report and the insurance approval are separate processes — filing with the carrier does not automatically start an insurance claim.

sections.title: The 21-day rule and contact
sections.text: Baggage not found within 21 days is treated as lost. Note: this 21-day period defines when baggage counts as lost — it is not the deadline for filing a written claim. For general queries, the Global Contact Centre is at +91 124 693 5600, but this is a remote centre, not a direct PIR line. File the PIR at the airport desk itself. Specific desk numbers, phone numbers and hours for Varanasi (VNS), Pune (PNQ) and Bangkok (BKK) are not confirmed on official channels.

actions.label: Air India Express Terms and Conditions

faq.q: My bag did not arrive on my Air India Express flight. What should I do first?
faq.a: Go to the Baggage Desk before leaving the arrival airport and file a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) with supporting documents. Do not leave the airport first and report later.

faq.q: What documents should I keep?
faq.a: Keep your baggage tag, a copy of the PIR, your boarding pass, and receipts for essential purchases. You will need these for the airline process and separately for any insurance claim.

faq.q: My bag has been missing for 21 days. What happens now?
faq.a: Baggage not found within 21 days is treated as lost. This 21-day period is the point at which baggage counts as lost — it is not the same as the deadline for filing a written claim, so check the applicable claim timelines separately.

faq.q: Can I file the PIR by calling +91 124 693 5600?
faq.a: The Global Contact Centre handles general queries and is not listed as a direct PIR line. File your arrival baggage report at the airport Baggage Desk with supporting documents.
